orientation.batter_faces: East-southeast. PNC Park has a 120-degree orientation - center field points east-southeast, so a batter standing at home plate faces roughly ESE (~120 degrees). Home plate sits at the northwest corner of the site. Consequences: downtown Pittsburgh, the Roberto Clemente Bridge and the Allegheny River lie beyond right field / right-center, so the best skyline sightlines are from the third-base side and left field looking back across the diamond (this is also why the Pirates' home dugout was placed on the third-base side). The first-base side gets afternoon shade from the upper deck; the third-base side and the left-field stands take the setting sun.
orientation.source: https://theshadium.com/blog/shaded-seats-pnc-park (120-degree orientation, CF points ESE); corroborated by https://ballparkeguides.com/pnc-park-seating-guide/ (home plate in the northwest corner; setting sun blinds the left-field stands and third-base side) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PNC_Park (home dugout on third-base line for the skyline view)

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers increase from the RIGHT FIELD / FIRST BASE side toward the THIRD BASE / LEFT FIELD side, then continue around the outfield from left field through center field and end in right field - i.e. a full loop. On the 100 Level: 101 is at the right-field end, numbers climb up the first-base line to 116/117 directly behind home plate, continue down the third-base line (125) into the left-field corner (131-132), across the left-field bleachers (133-138, bullpens beside 138), through center field (139-140) and finish as right-field Outfield Reserved (141-147). The Field Level (1-32) follows the same direction: low numbers on the first-base/right-field side, 14-19 behind home plate, high numbers (30-32) at the left-field corner. The 200 and 300 Levels mirror it (201-205 right-field line, 216-217 behind the plate, 235-238 left-field bleachers).

accessibility.summary: The Pirates provide ADA/wheelchair-accessible seating in more than 45 sections spread across every level and price point, from the upper deck to premium behind-the-plate locations, with adjacent companion seats. Buy through pirates.com using the 'Need ADA Seats?' / 'Click here for real-time ADA/Handicap Seating' filter on the interactive seat map, by phone at (412) 321-2827 or 1-800-BUY-BUCS, or in person; existing tickets can be exchanged for accessible locations at any ticket window or at the Main Guest Relations Office at the bottom of the Home Plate Rotunda. Complimentary general admission is provided for government-funded personal care attendants (PCAs) for guests with severe disabilities, arranged at time of purchase. Ushers will roll or fold removable seats on arrival. Specific locations noted: Field Level section 1 has wheelchair seating in front of Row D; 100 Level section 127 (third-base side) is weather-protected by the upper-deck overhang, which also slightly restricts the high view; section 141 in right-center offers a strong sightline with removable wheeled seats and fixed companion seating; an 'OF-WC' outfield wheelchair area has safety netting (seats 59-82 have the weaker sightlines); Grandstand section 317 behind home plate is noted for the skyline view. Accessible parking is in the lots surrounding PNC Park (ALCO Parking, 412-323-4455). The Center Field Gate is an accessible entry point.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE LETTERS at PNC Park, not numbers - CONFIRMED across every level. Field Level: e.g. section 1 = rows A-C then D-M; section 32 = rows F-M; Home Plate Club sections 14-19 = rows A-M. 100 Level Infield Box: rows A-Z then double letters AA-KK (section 117 has 53 rows A-Z, AA-KK; section 116 = A-Z, AA-HH; section 101 = A-Z, AA-GG). Left-field bleachers: section 133 = rows A-P. 200 Level Pittsburgh Baseball Club: short sections, rows A-K, with the entrance tunnel at Row D. 200 Level bleachers: section 236 = rows A-R. 300 Level Grandstand: lettered with gaps where the entrance vomitory cuts through - section 317 = rows D, H-R. Section 339 (Rooftop) = rows A-C with the entrance at Row C. SEAT NUMBERING: seat 1 in each section is on the side adjacent to the next LOWER-numbered section, and seat numbers climb toward the next higher-numbered section (e.g. in section 116, seat 1 is nearest section 115). Because PNC's section numbers climb from the right-field/first-base side toward the third-base/left-field side, this means that for a fan seated and facing the field, seat 1 is generally on the RIGHT-hand side of the section (the first-base side) - UNCERTAIN, this last inference is derived rather than sourced. Sources: https://www.tickpick.com/blog/pittsburgh-pirates-seating-chart-with-seat-views/ , https://www.simpleseats.com/pnc-park-seating-chart/ , individual rateyourseats section pages.
discovery.known_obstructions: 1) PROTECTIVE NETTING: there is netting or screening in front of 100 Level Infield Box sections 109-124 (netting was extended in recent seasons); the height and thickness of the screen varies section to section - CONFIRMED (rateyourseats section 116/117 fan feedback). 2) UPPER-DECK OVERHANG: on the 100 Level, rows W and above are under cover - great for shade/rain but it clips the view of high fly balls and the videoboard; wheelchairtravel specifically flags section 127 as protected-but-view-restricted by the overhang - CONFIRMED. 3) ROBERTO CLEMENTE WALL: the 21-foot right-field wall means fans in the right-field seats cannot see balls played off the wall below them - CONFIRMED. 4) UPPER-DECK GLASS STAIRWAY LANDINGS: ballparkeguides reports that several upper-level sections (313, 315 and others) have views partially obstructed by glass stairway landings - PLAUSIBLE but NOT independently confirmed; the rateyourseats pages for 313 and 315 carry no obstruction warning. 5) SCOREBOARD HEAD-TURN (not an obstruction but a sightline quirk): outfield and corner sections require a near-180-degree turn to see the main videoboard - explicitly noted for Field Level sections 30-32 and for the left-field bleachers (133-138, 235-238), which sit directly beneath/in front of the board. 6) SUN: the third-base side and the left-field stands take the setting sun; the first-base side is the shaded side for afternoon games.
